problem_keywords: infrastructure fault misclassified as review fault
propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang in the snapshot code (repo_snapshot.py:337-393) times out after 300s and raises SnapshotFetchError, which is caught by adapter.code_review_decision's blanket exception handler and misclassified as a review fault, causing a spurious LLM-Review -1 vote to be posted.

The spurious -1 vote removes the change from backfill reconciliation permanently because reconcile.py pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote and already_voted, so changes with any LLM-Review vote are skipped on subsequent passes.

The design correctly handles hung reviews one layer up (app.py:161-176, reconcile.py:222-226 abandon without voting), but the inner adapter/voter layer inconsistently votes -1 on infrastructure faults instead of abstaining and leaving the change vote-less for backfill retry.

A narrow classifier is needed to distinguish retryable infrastructure faults (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) from genuine review conclusions, routing faults to an ABSTAIN result that posts no vote and writes no dedup row.
An abstained change must remain vote-less so the backfill reconciler's has_llm_review_vote pre-filter re-picks it on the next pass, restoring self-healing behavior.

The inner git timeout (300s) always fires before the outer review timeout (1200s), so infrastructure stalls are structurally guaranteed to take the vote-bearing path and never the benign no-vote path that already exists upstream.
